title: Lightweight performance-profile diffs and fast pin-rollbacks
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: Publishing a full Redwood-verified performance profile (latency/throughput/cost) currently requires re-running a full verification harness and storing a complete profile artifact. For small, well-understood changes (e.g., quantization flag flip, kernel selection tweak, minor batching delta) this is heavyweight and slows rollouts and rollbacks. Goal: introduce a lightweight delta/diff format for performance profiles plus a fast pin-override and rollback mechanism so small changes can be published and reverted with minimal verification cost while maintaining auditability and safety.
background: Existing workflows: automated sample-driven verification (PM-76840) and pinned profile publish (PM-31608) produce canonical JSON profile artifacts stored in the registry. Operators currently create canaries by publishing new full profiles and waiting for canary telemetry; rollback requires re-publishing the previous full profile and re-running gating. This ticket proposes an incremental diff format combined with a signed lightweight canary publish path and an emergency pin-override API to speed rollback and reduce verification compute for minor changes.
acceptance_criteria: Define a compact profile diff format that encodes: changed metrics, normalized cost delta, provenance (base profile id+signature), and minimum verification sample set
Runtime can apply a profile diff on top of an existing pinned profile and produce a runnable profile within the serving control plane within 5s

Publish pipeline supports a 'fast-publish' mode that signs diffs and stores them in the registry; fast-publish requires a smaller verification harness (<= 25% of full samples) but must record gating telemetry
Console shows diffs in the profile comparison view with clear flag for 'fast publish' and a button to execute emergency pin-rollback to previous full profile
Security & audit logs contain a signed chain (base profile -> diff -> applied runtime state) and can be used to reconstruct the full profile artifact for a given commit
Canary telemetry must automatically escalate to full verification if drift or regression thresholds exceed defined tolerances
tasks: PM: finalize diff schema and gating thresholds with runtime and research
ENG-runtime: implement diff-apply logic and verification-lite harness endpoint
ENG-orchestration: add registry storage for diffs and signed provenance links
ENG-console: UI to visualize diffs and expose emergency rollback button
SRE: create SLOs/alerts for fast-publish canaries and escalation paths
Docs: publish publishing playbook and developer guide for fast-publish
Security: review signing workflow and RBAC for pin-override API
notes_updates: 2025-01-15 - Ticket created by Asha: proposal based on runtime perf backlog and customer feedback from two mid-market customers requesting faster rollback paths

2025-01-21 - Sync: defined initial diff shape with Runtime (Marcus Li, Priya Rao). Key decision: diffs are additive and reference a single base profile id; we will not support merging two independent diffs in this phase

2025-01-28 - Engineering kickoff: ENG-runtime prototype for diff-apply completed (branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/compare/diff-apply-proto PR#824). Prototype applies diffs in ~1.8s on ci-gpu-1 with minimal memory overhead

2025-01-30 - Design feedback (console): need clear UX to indicate 'fast-publish' risk and provide link to telemetry stream. Design mock attached in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/perf-diff-ui
2025-02-04 - Security review notes: signing chain OK, but RBAC for emergency pin-override must require 2-person approval or an org-level emergency key. Security assigned follow-up ENG-Sec-103

2025-02-06 - Runtime bench: reduced verification sample set for 'fast-publish' passes stable workloads; regression guard rails defined: latency P95 increase <= 7%, throughput drop <= 6%, cost delta <= 12% (relative to base).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fast-publish diffs may mask larger regressions not covered by small sample sets. Mitigation: automatic escalation to full verification when telemetry crosses thresholds + conservative default thresholds

Risk: Confusing UX could lead operators to publish diffs where full publish is required. Mitigation: add pre-publish checklist, locked default to require explicit checkbox and show expected cost/regression trade-offs

Risk: Signed chain complexity increases audit and storage needs. Mitigation: store diffs as deltas and make full-profile reconstruction a background job; enforce TTL for historical diffs and archive full artifacts in cold storage
Risk: Emergency pin-override misuse. Mitigation: require 2-step approval and RBAC; log and alert every override with linked justification
